subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Wheatstone Bridge: Precision Measurement
description: A quick win: understand Wheatstone Bridge: Precision Measurement.

hook.text: How do you measure a tiny change in resistance? Balance a bridge and watch it tip.

buildup.text: Four resistors form a diamond. A meter reads the voltage across the middle.

discovery.text: When balanced, the meter reads zero. Any imbalance reveals the unknown resistance.

twist.text: Strain gauges use Wheatstone bridges — tiny deformation changes resistance detectably.

climax.text: Every digital scale and load cell uses this 1843 invention daily.

punchline.text: Balance the bridge and the invisible becomes measurable.

quiz.question: How does a Wheatstone bridge measure resistance?
options: It measures the current through a single resistor
It detects voltage imbalance in a four-resistor diamond circuit
It compares resistance to a fixed voltage standard
